extra.reason: Gate landed in the thinker fork: Config.llm_factions bitmask (default 0 = stock behaviour), llm_endpoint, and llm_enabled() alongside thinker_enabled. Mode B+ recommended and documented at the option in thinker.ini. Verified by MinGW cross-compile to a PE32 DLL. Intercepting an actual decision is A1 (na-61c).

Ledger derived, not tabulated: orchestrator/src/neural_amplifier/fairness.py computes the fairness block from (slot, difficulty, thinker.ini config) across all 15 entries, each citing its file:line in the fork. Reading the source corrected the game-surface.md table in four places -- tech_cost_factor and content_pop flip sides at Librarian, combat modifiers favour the human not the AI, and unit_support_bonus is inert under shipped defaults. handicap_drift() catches an adapter whose stamp disagrees (missing/unexpected/mislabelled); coverage gained fair_play and structural_handicaps so the claim is measured. 25 new tests. Adapter-side stamping is A1 (na-61c).

Layer 2 landed in orchestrator/src/neural_amplifier/telemetry.py. Emitter takes the already-built DecisionRecord and hands the same instance to every sink, so 'assembled once' is structural -- the test asserts object identity, not field equality. DecisionLog is just the first sink and is written first, so an exporter failure still leaves the record of truth on disk; sinks never raise into the decision loop and failures are counted on Emitter.failures and surfaced at GET /health. OtelSink continues the adapter's W3C traceparent rather than starting a new trace (dependency-free strict parser, 10 malformed cases rejected), reconstructs span timing from latency_ms since the decision is already over, sets ERROR status on degradation, and emits the section 6 metrics with a bounded-cardinality attribute subset. Enabled with NA_OTEL=1 and the otel extra. 27 new tests against an in-memory tracer -- no collector, no game. Also fixed a real crash path: _record read world_view.trace.traceparent, which AttributeErrors on a model_copy-constructed view and would stall the game after the decision; now WorldView.traceparent() tolerates both shapes.

Negative result: auto_play_callback is NOT the unattended driver. Zero call sites in the fork (engine.cpp:638 declares the pointer, nothing invokes it), and 0x50E890 sits inside a contiguous block of void(int) GUI timer callbacks -- mandate_color 0x50E820, then blink_timer 0x50EA40, blink2_timer, line_timer, turn_timer (its int annotated 'unused'), go_timer. Siblings are patched at GUI offsets and reimplemented in gui.cpp (mod_blink_timer, mod_turn_timer at patch.cpp:445,1158). This is SMAC's attract-mode/animation tick; the name is misleading. headless-harness.md section 7 Q2 updated to say so and to point at load_daemon + cmd_parse + mod_auto_save instead.

Gated orchestrator-side in fog.py. redact() drops any delta naming a faction outside the world view's new contacts list, before the brain call -- a redaction applied after the prompt would be theatre, and the test asserts the brain never saw it. Deltas naming no parties are public news and survive; the viewing faction is implicitly contacted. Removals are counted on the decision record (redacted_deltas) and aggregated in coverage, so a leaking adapter shows up as a number rather than as a suspiciously well-informed run. A world view without contacts sets fog_enforced=false rather than reporting clean -- we cannot distinguish a legitimate delta from a leaked one, so absence of evidence is recorded as such. Contract gained contacts; headless-harness.md section 4.2 documents the gate. 10 tests. Adapter-side filtering at mod_NetMsg_pop is still the right first line and belongs with A1.

Machinery landed and tested; recording a real game is na-oh5. Dropped the na-04z dependency: the replay path needs stored world views, not an adapter that stamps surface_id -- that was a mis-specified blocker. replay.WorldViewStore is content-addressed by the record's own world_view_hash (the blocker found on starting was that the record carries only the hash and nothing kept the bytes, so a log alone could never be replayed). Two verdicts kept separate: deterministic (exact, scripted only) and consistent (no new degradation, same surfaces fired) -- the trap is a replay where the fallback happens to pick what the brain picked. Wired as NA_WORLD_VIEW_STORE, 'neural-amplifier replay' and 'just replay', plus stored() for fixture harvesting.

Landed less the Quipu round-trip. datalinks/ parses alphax.txt deterministically (no model: it is fixed-arity CSV with inline column docs, and a hallucinated tech prerequisite tagged canonical is the worst failure available to us), emits the smac: graph with all three anti-masquerade predicates on every node, and serves a static briefing plus action-space-scoped grounding through the Retriever seam. Verified against a real 1281-line alphax.txt: 88 techs, 133 facilities (50 Disabled), 64 SP rows, 2579 triples round-tripping through rdflib. Three bugs found by checking rather than eyeballing: (1) two facilities have commas inside effect text, so SP detection had to move from row arity to 'last five fields are ints'; (2) Turtle PN_LOCAL forbids '/', so smac:tech/biogen was a parse error that looked perfectly reasonable -- fixed with per-class prefixes and rdflib is now a dev dep gating it; (3) Disable in a preq column means excluded-from-game, not a prerequisite, and treating it as a tech would have invented 50 fake edges. Also: alphax.txt's own header calls the facility column 'Free' (grants the facility free at new bases), not obsoletedBy as knowledge-architecture.md says -- the file wins, noted in rdf.py. Added NA_EXTRACTION_MODEL (default claude-haiku-4-5) as a separate cheaper dial from the brain's, for K3's postgame episode extraction which IS genuine model work. Remaining: load the graph into a running Quipu and serve retrieval from it rather than the parsed structs -- folded into na-6ce (K2). 21 tests against a synthetic excerpt; the real alphax.txt is game data and is never committed.
